title: mine evidence to extend US_STATES for France
headline: FR_REGIONS coverage is fine, but the '100% of France rows' denominator behind that clearance is test_s1 only: across all three test splits 43,411 of 1,694,445 France rows (2.5620%) cannot carry a state, a hard ceiling of 97.4380%. The real France dictionary gap is in ADDR_CANON_FR, not FR_REGIONS: six France-only address tokens (ge 41,120; pr 5,881; cit 5,580; cite 2,546; haut 2,263; es 2,168) are unhandled, and LEET corrupts 1,111 French ordinal name tokens (3eme->eeme, 1er->ler) while correctly decoding 1,949 genuine leetspeak tokens.
most_important_number_meaning: France rows with an empty business_address across test_s1+s2+s3 (2.5423% of 1,694,445 France rows); these can never resolve a state, so the true state-resolution ceiling is 97.4380%, not the 100.00% quoted in REFUTED-2

scope.why: France appears only in test; country_rows in train_s1, train_s2, train_s3 contains no 'France' key

already_checked_interaction.refuted_1_pin_guard: not re-derived; out of scope for this dictionary task

refuted_2_fr_regions.status: conclusion CONFIRMED by independent evidence, but denominator is too narrow
refuted_2_fr_regions.independent_confirmation: FR_REGIONS canonical values hdf/idf/naq/pdl each occur 0 times in the France address token stream, so the missing self-map loop at normalize.py:252 is inert
refuted_2_fr_regions.scope_correction: the quoted 259,452/259,452 equals exactly the test_s1 France row count; it is a test_s1-only measurement
refuted_2_fr_regions.denominator_caveat: any 'state resolves for X% of France' claim must state its split

F0_state_resolution_ceiling.arithmetic_invariant: rows - addr_empty == has_comma + nonempty_comma_free  (holds exactly for every split x country)
F0_state_resolution_ceiling.code_evidence: normalize_address('', 'France') -> state='' ; normalize_address('Nord','France') -> state='hdf' (so a comma-free row can only resolve if the whole address is a bare region name)
F0_state_resolution_ceiling.verdict: the empty-address rate is a source-2/3 data property matching US and India, NOT a France defect; it bounds the achievable rate only

F1_region_candidates_not_in_FR_REGIONS.note: FR_REGIONS has 14 keys covering 4 canonical values (hdf, naq, pdl, idf)
F1_region_candidates_not_in_FR_REGIONS.caveat: normalize_address matches a region only when an ENTIRE comma-component equals a key; a token count is not a row count and not a state-signal count. build_profile.py flattens tokens per component so component identity is lost. Hence LIKELY not CONFIRMED.

candidates.rationale: prefixes general (4826 -> canon 'gen') and gen (1227 -> 'gen'); also prefixes georges (10957), george (1361), germain (950)

address_ordinals_unhandled.note: survive as literals in addresses because LEET is not applied there, and none is in any canon dict

F4_fused_building_suffixes.defect: fused <n>b / <n>bis tokens are neither split nor canon-mapped, so '12 bis' and '12bis' produce different token streams

gaps.gap: Accented French place names are invisible to the profile: build_profile.py uses TOKEN_RE=[a-z0-9]+ and never strips accents, so 'Vende'+'e' tokenises as 'vend'+'e'
gaps.evidence: vendee=0 but vend=230; rhone, pyrenees, finistere, herault, lozere, cotes all exactly 0
gaps.consequence: zero counts are a measurement artefact, not evidence of absence; no accented department can be ranked or ruled out; this is why no F1 row is CONFIRMED
gaps.not_a_pipeline_bug: strip_accents runs before matching in normalize.py; verified 'Vende'->'vendee'->state='pdl'

gaps.gap: Component identity is lost: addr_tokens is flattened per [,;] component, so a region component cannot be told apart from a street-name token
gaps.consequence: F1 candidates capped at LIKELY; unfixable without a re-scan

gaps.gap: Top-4000 truncation floor per country per file: rank-4000 count is 23/58/60 (address) and 9/25/26 (name) for test_s1/2/3
gaps.consequence: absence of a low-count candidate is not evidence of absence; 2eme=0 in name_tokens is inside the floor and inconclusive

gaps.gap: city_comps and address component-order behaviour are not measured at all by the profile
gaps.consequence: the region-before-city vs city-before-region inconsistency flagged in the work order was not tested

gaps.gap: No per-row data; every rate is token-occurrence-based and row-level rates for the F1 candidates are unknown
The earlier '~1,100 rows of legacy names' figure could not be verified: no profile field records it, and F1's 10,387 token occurrences cannot be converted to rows
